history.title: Army of Bombay → Bombay: success; 0 officer losses.
history.report:
13 dice after 1 defence. Committed: 12 regiments, 2 officers; alliances: none.

Exhaust 12 regiments, 2 officers and 0 local alliances. Return 0 lost officers to their players’ supplies. Never remove regiments for this loss check.

Distribute £8 loot: Commander £1 plus £1 per own surviving officer, then clockwise £1 per surviving officer. Pay the bank £1 per regiment and alliance. Repeat while cash remains; stop when it runs out.

Take 1 trophies; remove the target’s tower and dome. Open all its orders and remove all its unrest.

Move Bombay’s loot/control token, region side faceup, above the Bombay President. Place its Governor overlay and put its Governor card in Vacant Offices.

lines.text: The dispute had been settled by force of arms, a method of negotiation in which the Company had recently acquired considerable confidence.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “The Company believes this matter concluded. I admire its confidence.”
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: “The territory is taken. Keeping it may prove less straightforward.”
lines.speaker: Thomas Finch

history.title: Bombay · Tax 1 this turn
history.report:
Resolve the successful Tax’s £2 payment on the table.

First Tax in Bombay this turn: add no unrest. Later Taxes in this region add one unrest each.

lines.text: Bombay: Tax recorded; 0 unrest added.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “They took the kingdom. Now they send the bill.”
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: “A most encouraging result. The natives have demonstrated a remarkable willingness to contribute to their own improvement.”
lines.speaker: Edward Avery

history.title: Bombay · Tax 2 this turn
history.report:
Resolve the successful Tax’s £2 payment on the table.

Add 1 unrest to Bombay (now 1).

lines.text: The Company had expected gratitude, or at least obedience. The inhabitants, demonstrating their usual difficulty with administrative terminology, appeared to have confused both with resentment.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: Another Tax in Bombay. The demand is familiar; familiarity has not made it welcome.
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: The Tax has been recorded. The payment remains a matter for the physical table.
lines.speaker: Edward Avery

history.title: Manual event test · Leader
history.report:
Bombay attack: 0 base + 1 unrest × 1 = 1. Exhaust available Army strength 1; attack repelled.

Remove all 1 unrest from Bombay.

The associated Commander, if occupied, takes one trophy for defending Bombay.

Manual test: the digital event stack and phase event count are unchanged. Use Undo to reverse this test’s board effects.

lines.text: The rebellion had failed. Its causes, being considerably more difficult to defeat than its participants, remained.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: The attack on Bombay has been repelled. For the moment, our arrangements remain.
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: “We have suppressed the rebellion. That does not mean we have settled the matter.”
lines.speaker: Thomas Finch

lines.text: The Company's latest initiative had failed. Fortunately, its administrative structure ensured that responsibility could be distributed so widely that nobody was required to accept any.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: The Company took control of Bombay. This administrative setback gives our court another reason to remember.
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: “The policy was perfectly sound. Its implementation was regrettably entrusted to people who attempted to carry it out.”
lines.speaker: Edward Avery

history.title: Manual event test · Leader
history.report:
Bombay attack: 0 base + 1 unrest × 1 = 1. Exhaust available Army strength 0; insufficient defence.

Bombay is lost. Army of Bombay: if the Commander office is occupied, return half that family’s trophies (round up) and remove the Commander; roll one die per officer in the Army and remove each officer rolling 6.

Officer rout · Bombay · Army of Bombay: 0 officers removed (reported from the table).

Return the Governor of Bombay card to unused offices, its officeholder and fatigue to supply, and remove its overlay.

Remove any unfinished Company ship; return Bombay’s control token to the region loot-side facedown. Lower Company Standing by 1 spaces for this turn’s 1st region loss.

Remove all 1 unrest from Bombay.

Restore Bombay’s dome with one tower level.

Close Bombay £3 (northern). Return any writer there to its owner; flip any filled-order token.

Close Bombay £3 (middle). Return any writer there to its owner; flip any filled-order token.

Close Bombay £4 (southern). Return any writer there to its owner; flip any filled-order token.

Manual test: the digital event stack and phase event count are unchanged. Use Undo to reverse this test’s board effects.

lines.text: The Company had lost control of the territory. Its officials were expected to describe the development as temporary, although the inhabitants appeared determined to make it permanent.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “The Company was very eager to explain why my kingdom no longer belonged to me. I look forward to hearing its explanation of why it no longer belongs to them.”
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: Bombay has been lost. The physical reports record the Army consequences; they do not tell us the fate of every person.
lines.speaker: Thomas Finch

history.title: Army of Bombay → Bombay: failure; 0 officer losses.
history.report:
13 dice after 1 defence. Committed: 12 regiments, 2 officers; alliances: none.

Exhaust 12 regiments, 2 officers and 0 local alliances. Return 0 lost officers to their players’ supplies. Never remove regiments for this loss check.

Region control, orders, unrest and Elephant position stay as they were.

lines.text: The expedition had been undertaken with every expectation of success. The Company's expectations, unfortunately, had not been consulted by the enemy.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “Their previous success appears to have encouraged certain unfortunate assumptions.”
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: “We failed. I suggest we begin with that fact, however unpleasant the gentlemen in London may find it.”
lines.speaker: Thomas Finch
